Turning Off

If you do not want to drive straight on at an intersection but turn left or right, a number of traffic rules apply. You must give way to many more road users than when driving straight on. Always take road users in the blind spot into account.

Blind Spot

The area next to and diagonally behind the vehicle that you cannot see through the mirrors. This area can only be overlooked by turning your head and looking closely. In larger vehicles, blind spots are bigger and more are added — such as directly behind and just in front of the vehicle.

Giving Way

Once at the intersection, the following rules apply:

📍 Rule 1 — Oncoming traffic on the same road

You must give way to oncoming traffic on the same road — including pedestrians!

📍 Rule 2 — Through traffic next to or behind you

You must give way to through traffic next to you or behind you — including pedestrians!

↩️ Rule 3 — Short turn goes before long turn

If oncoming drivers want to drive the same way as you do, the driver who turns right will go in front of the driver who turns left.

↪️
Short Turn — Right

Turning right is the shorter path. This driver goes first.

↩️
Long Turn — Left

Turning left is the longer path. This driver must wait.

🚃 Rule 4 — Turning tram has right of way

A turning tram has right of way over all traffic the tram approaches from the front, or that is next to it, or diagonally behind it.

Divergent Priority Road

Some priority roads do not go straight, but curve. These divergent priority roads must be seen as the main road. If you go off this road, it is called turning off — only then do the rules "through traffic before turning traffic" and "short turn goes before long turn" apply.

This can be confusing because of the bend. Try to think of the entire priority road as a straight road in your head, with one or more side roads. Drivers on the divergent priority road are, seen from the side road, crossing drivers — they have priority over drivers from the side road.

💡 Although continuing on a divergent priority road does not constitute a turn, you are expected to indicate direction so other road users can see you are staying on the road.

Divergent priority roads are usually indicated with supplementary plates under the "priority road" or "priority intersection" sign. The thick line shows the divergent priority road; thin lines show side roads that must give way.

B-1 + supplementary plate
Divergent priority road to the left with two side roads.
B-4 + supplementary plate
Divergent priority road to the right with one side road.
